purpose: VibeVoice-ASR Q4_K_M decode: route rows=1 through the raw-block pack8 decode GEMV families
hardware: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ PRO 395, Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), 256-bit LPDDR5X, 133 GB unified

protocol.weights: Q4_K_M backbone (168 Q4_K + 28 Q6_K layer tensors), bf16 front-end + dense bf16 untied lm_head
protocol.kernels: gguf_q4_k_pack8_gemv_decode_* / gguf_q6_k_pack8_gemv_decode_* read the unmodified GGUF block bytes on device; no repack, no sidecar, no extra resident memory
protocol.workload: Qwen2 backbone decode at ~150-token context, 3 warmup steps, 3 timed trials of 40 steps
protocol.command: python3 - <<'EOF' (load /tmp/vibevoice-asr-q4km.gguf, prompt from tests/fixtures/vibevoice_asr/vibevoice_asr_lm.npz, time push_token+forward_layers+logits_argmax loops) EOF

gates.gpu_suite: 7/7 tests/test_gpu_vibevoice_qwen2_q4_runner.py incl. greedy chain 16/16 vs torch fixture and first-position logits top-1
gates.weight_type_routing: all 196 layer GEMM weights still route to K-quant blocks the kernels own
gates.wer_recheck: 20-clip Q4 WER lane in flight at time of writing; the 50-clip gate remains 1.978% == bf16 1.978%

notes: The naive per-column raw-block GEMVs run at 18-60 GB/s; the pack8 decode families reach 107-132 GB/s, which is the bandwidth wall for these shapes (dense bf16 streams 14.15 GB/token in 66 ms = 214 GB/s).
The 5.01 GB/token stream is 3.92 GB of layer GEMM weights plus a 1.09 GB dense bf16 lm_head; the lm_head is 6.6 ms of the 49.4 ms and already runs at ~210 GB/s.

A single-GEMV speedup does not transfer one-for-one: the microbenchmark projected 39.1 ms/token and the integrated decode measures 49.4 ms. The difference is the per-token non-GEMM work (196 GEMM launches plus ~336 norm/rotary/KV/attention/residual/silu launches per token) and context-dependent attention.
Prefill is unchanged and remains the dominant cost: 89 rows through the row-by-row path measured 3.80 s (~43 ms/row).
